subtitle: The intelligence brief on models, agents & shipping AI products
footer_tagline: Curated for AI product managers navigating the model layer.
audience: AI product managers at startups and enterprises who own roadmaps with LLM, agent, or ML-powered features. They follow model releases and benchmark news but need signal filtered for product decisions, not research. They want to know what changed, why it matters to their roadmap, and what competitors are shipping — without wading through hype or academic minutiae.
in_scope: Foundation model releases, capability jumps, and deprecations (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Mistral, etc.)
AI agent frameworks, tool-use patterns, and multi-agent orchestration
AI product launches and feature announcements from major platforms (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, Meta)
Inference cost, latency, and context-window changes that affect product economics
Emerging UX patterns and design paradigms for AI-native products
AI safety, alignment, and policy developments that affect what can be shipped
Developer tooling: evals, observability, fine-tuning, RAG, and prompt engineering advances
Enterprise AI adoption signals, case studies, and procurement trends
out_scope: Chip fabrication, semiconductor supply chain, and hardware deep-dives (audience is not hardware PMs)
Pure academic ML research with no near-term product relevance
General SaaS product management advice not specific to AI
Crypto, Web3, or blockchain unless directly intersecting with AI product decisions
Consumer gadget reviews and consumer electronics news
relevance_gate: Would an AI PM change their roadmap, model choice, or product strategy after reading this?

tracks.name: Model Layer
tracks.desc: New model releases, capability benchmarks, context windows, multimodality, and deprecation notices from frontier and open-weight labs.

tracks.name: Agents & Tooling
tracks.desc: Agent frameworks, tool-use APIs, orchestration patterns, evals infrastructure, and observability — the plumbing AI PMs actually build on.

tracks.name: Competitive Moves
tracks.desc: Feature launches, platform pivots, and partnership announcements from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, Meta, and fast-moving challengers.

tracks.name: Product Economics
tracks.desc: Inference pricing changes, rate limits, latency improvements, and cost-per-token shifts that directly affect build-vs-buy and margin decisions.

tracks.name: Policy & Safety
tracks.desc: Regulation, usage policy updates, model cards, red-team findings, and compliance signals that constrain or unlock what teams can ship.

tracks.name: UX & Adoption
tracks.desc: Emerging AI-native interaction patterns, enterprise rollout case studies, and user research on how people actually use AI features.

tone: Direct, practitioner-to-practitioner — concrete implications over breathless hype, always answering 'so what does this mean for my product?'
